newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst looks to shed accident-prone image.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst looks to shed accident-prone image.

text.p: Hoechst AG, seeking to polish its image tarnished by recent chemical spills, on Monday launched a campaign to revamp its reputation after a survey showed nearly nine out of ten people associated it with accidents.

The Frankfurt-based chemicals and drugs group said a public poll showed that 88 percent of the respondents linked the group to chemical accidents, adding that Hoechst had the worst public standing among all the major German chemical groups.
"The group plans to inform the public without gaps" when accidents occur, Hoechst management board member Ernst Schadow told a news conference.
Hoechst, Europe's largest chemicals group, became a target of public outrage in early 1996 when it reported three chemical spills at its suburban Frankfurt facility in only four days.
The accidents prompted the state of Hesse to shut down two plant units where the accidents occurred.

A toxic chemical powder dusted a suburban Frankfurt neighbourhood Frankfurt in one accident, while another accident caused the release of some 1.5 tonnes of an intermediary substance in a painkiller to seep into the Main River.
But Hoechst said the poll also showed that 51 percent of those surveyed favoured keeping chemical companies in suburban areas -- as long as the safety precautions were stringent.
Hoechst plans to publish a magazine once a year with articles written by independent journalists about the environment and to detail safety precautions on CD-ROM.
